project.name: evolve-framework
project.description: A research-grade evolutionary algorithms experimentation framework

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the unified configuration module, re-exporting UnifiedConfig and every sub-config (stopping, callbacks, ERP, multi-objective, meta-evolution, tracking) as the public config API.

nodes.name: callbacks.py
nodes.summary: Defines the frozen CallbackConfig dataclass that declaratively enables built-in logging and checkpointing callbacks, with validation and dict round-tripping.

nodes.name: CallbackConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen config enabling built-in logging (level, destination) and checkpointing (directory, frequency) callbacks, with validation and to_dict/from_dict.

nodes.name: erp.py
nodes.summary: Defines ERPSettings, the frozen config for Evolvable Reproduction Protocol runs (step limit, recovery threshold, protocol mutation rate, intent/recovery toggles); its presence makes the factory build an ERPEngine.

nodes.name: ERPSettings
nodes.summary: Frozen ERP settings (step limit, recovery threshold, protocol mutation rate, intent/recovery flags) whose presence switches the factory to ERPEngine.

nodes.name: merge.py
nodes.summary: Defines MergeConfig, the frozen config for the symbiogenetic merge phase (operator, merge rate, symbiont source/fate, archive and interface sizing, weight initialization) inserted after variation.

nodes.name: MergeConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen config for the symbiogenetic merge phase with validated rates, symbiont source/fate, archive and interface sizing, and weight initialization options.

nodes.name: meta.py
nodes.summary: Defines meta-evolution configuration: ParameterSpec describes how one config path maps to genome dimensions (continuous/integer/categorical, bounds, log scale) and MetaEvolutionConfig sets the outer-loop population, generations, trials and aggregation.

nodes.name: ParameterSpec
nodes.summary: Describes one evolvable config parameter by dotted path and type (continuous, integer, categorical) with bounds, choices and log scale, and reports its genome dimension count.

nodes.name: MetaEvolutionConfig
nodes.summary: Outer-loop meta-evolution settings: evolvable parameter specs, outer population size and generations, trials per config, aggregation method and optional inner generation override.

nodes.name: multiobjective.py
nodes.summary: Defines multi-objective configuration: ObjectiveSpec (name, direction, weight), ConstraintSpec (penalty weight) and MultiObjectiveConfig (objectives, reference point, dominance vs penalty constraint handling) for NSGA-II runs.

nodes.name: ObjectiveSpec
nodes.summary: Specification of a single objective with name, minimize/maximize direction (default maximize for backward compatibility) and weight.

nodes.name: ConstraintSpec
nodes.summary: Specification of a named constraint and its penalty weight for penalty-based constraint handling.

nodes.name: MultiObjectiveConfig
nodes.summary: Multi-objective settings grouping objectives, an optional hypervolume reference point, constraints and the dominance or penalty constraint-handling mode.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Provides config schema versioning: a SemVer SchemaVersion type, a SchemaVersionError, a validator that rejects incompatible major versions and warns on minor mismatches, and a dict migration hook.

nodes.name: SchemaVersion
nodes.summary: Ordered SemVer value type with parsing, a current() constructor and major-version compatibility checks for config files.

nodes.name: SchemaVersionError
nodes.summary: Error raised when a configuration's schema version is incompatible with the running framework, carrying both versions.

nodes.name: validate_schema_version
nodes.summary: Validates a config's schema version against the current one, raising on major-version mismatch and warning (or raising in strict mode) on newer minor versions.

nodes.name: migrate_config_dict
nodes.summary: Migration hook that upgrades a config dict between schema versions; currently a pass-through placeholder for future migrations.

nodes.name: stopping.py
nodes.summary: Defines StoppingConfig, a frozen dataclass of optional stopping criteria (generation limit, fitness threshold, stagnation, time limit) where evolution halts when any criterion is met.

nodes.name: StoppingConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen set of optional stopping criteria that reports whether it is empty, iterates active criteria and round-trips to dicts.

nodes.name: tracking.py
nodes.summary: Declares experiment tracking configuration: a MetricCategory enum for metric granularity and a TrackingConfig dataclass (backend, URI, buffering, sampling, timing, dataset logging) with minimal/standard/comprehensive presets; deliberately free of ML-framework imports.

nodes.name: MetricCategory
nodes.summary: Enum of metric categories (core, extended stats, timing, diversity, ERP, multi-objective, metadata, derived analytics and similar) that gate what the tracker collects.

nodes.name: TrackingConfig
nodes.summary: Declarative tracking setup covering backend, experiment/run names, URI, metric categories, buffering and flush intervals, sampling and timing options, with category helpers and minimal/standard/comprehensive factory presets.

nodes.name: unified.py
nodes.summary: Central experiment specification: the frozen UnifiedConfig combines population, operator, genome, evaluator, decoder and all optional sub-configs into one JSON-serializable object with validation, file I/O, stable hashing and immutable with_* builders; DatasetConfig describes training/validation data.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses with dataclasses.replace-based with_* methods give an immutable builder API while keeping JSON round-tripping deterministic for hashing.

nodes.name: DatasetConfig
nodes.summary: Describes a named dataset (path, in-memory data, context) attached to a config as training or validation data, serializing only metadata.

nodes.name: UnifiedConfig
nodes.summary: Complete frozen experiment specification with mode predicates (ERP, multi-objective, meta, tracking, merge), JSON/file serialization with schema validation, SHA-256 hashing and immutable with_* builder methods.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry for tracking backends: re-exports the metric tracker classes and optionally exposes MLflow and Weights & Biases trackers behind availability flags.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses try/except ImportError to expose optional third-party backends only when installed.

nodes.name: is_mlflow_available
nodes.summary: Reports whether the optional MLflow tracker backend could be imported.

nodes.name: is_wandb_available
nodes.summary: Reports whether the optional Weights & Biases tracker backend could be imported.

nodes.name: callback.py
nodes.summary: Implements TrackingCallback, a late-priority engine callback that lazily builds a resilient MLflow tracker and logs per-generation metrics, flattened config params, tags, dataset metadata, config artifacts and the best solution, degrading to a no-op tracker when unavailable.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy ML dependencies are imported lazily inside methods so the core package stays importable without MLflow.

nodes.name: TrackingCallback
nodes.summary: Engine callback that lazily creates a resilient MLflow tracker on run start, logs generation metrics at the configured interval, records params, tags, datasets and config artifacts, and logs the best solution on run end or error.

nodes.name: _NullTracker
nodes.summary: No-op tracker used as a fallback when the tracking backend cannot be created.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for the engine factory, re-exporting create_engine, create_initial_population and OperatorCompatibilityError.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: Engine factory that turns a UnifiedConfig into a ready-to-run engine: resolves evaluators, decoders, operators, callbacks and genomes from the registries, validates operator-genome compatibility, builds stopping criteria, and chooses a standard, ERP or NSGA-II multi-objective engine.

nodes.name: OperatorCompatibilityError
nodes.summary: Raised when a configured operator is incompatible with the genome type, naming the operator, category and genome.

nodes.name: create_engine
nodes.summary: Main factory: resolves seed, decoder, evaluator (explicit or registry), operators and custom callbacks, validates compatibility, builds stopping criteria and dispatches to the standard, ERP or multi-objective engine builder.

nodes.name: _validate_operator_compatibility
nodes.summary: Checks each configured selection, crossover and mutation operator against the genome type using OperatorRegistry metadata and raises OperatorCompatibilityError on mismatch.

nodes.name: _build_stopping_criteria
nodes.summary: Builds a single or composite stopping criterion from max_generations and the optional StoppingConfig (fitness threshold, stagnation, time limit).

nodes.name: _build_callbacks
nodes.summary: Instantiates built-in logging, checkpoint and tracking callbacks from the config's callback and tracking settings.

nodes.name: _evolution_config
nodes.summary: Maps UnifiedConfig fields onto the core EvolutionConfig shared by all engine variants.

nodes.name: _create_standard_engine
nodes.summary: Constructs a standard EvolutionEngine from resolved operators, stopping, callbacks and optional merge settings.

nodes.name: _create_erp_engine
nodes.summary: Constructs an ERPEngine with ERPConfig derived from ERP settings, rejecting merge settings that ERP cannot honour.

nodes.name: _create_multiobjective_engine
nodes.summary: Constructs a multi-objective EvolutionEngine using crowded-tournament NSGA-II selection with objective directions and constraint handling from the config.

nodes.name: create_initial_population
nodes.summary: Creates a seeded initial Population by instantiating genomes from GenomeRegistry using the config's genome type and params.

nodes.name: evaluator.py
nodes.summary: Meta-evolution runtime: MetaEvaluator scores a candidate config by running seeded inner evolutionary trials and aggregating their fitness with caching, and run_meta_evolution drives the outer loop over encoded configs with tournament selection, crossover and mutation plus optional MLflow nested runs.

nodes.name: MetaEvaluator
nodes.summary: Evaluates a candidate UnifiedConfig by running deterministic seeded inner evolution trials, aggregating fitness by mean/median/best, caching results and optionally logging nested MLflow runs.

nodes.name: run_meta_evolution
nodes.summary: Runs the meta-evolution outer loop: encodes evolvable params with ConfigCodec, evolves candidate vectors, evaluates them via MetaEvaluator and returns a MetaEvolutionResult with the best config.

nodes.name: _tournament_select
nodes.summary: Tournament selection over (vector, fitness) pairs for the meta outer loop, honouring minimize.

nodes.name: _crossover_vectors
nodes.summary: Uniform crossover of two parameter vectors for the meta outer loop.

nodes.name: _mutate_vector
nodes.summary: Per-gene Gaussian mutation of a parameter vector for the meta outer loop.

nodes.name: accepts_keyword

nodes.name: reset_callback_registry

nodes.name: CallbackRegistry

nodes.name: reset_decoder_registry

nodes.name: DecoderRegistry
nodes.summary: Name-to-factory registry for decoders with lazy built-in initialization, registration, lookup and listing.

nodes.name: evaluators.py
nodes.summary: EvaluatorRegistry mapping names to evaluator factories, lazily registering benchmark, function, LLM-judge, ground-truth, SCM, RL and meta evaluators, and reporting which factories accept a given parameter.

nodes.name: _register_builtin_evaluators
nodes.summary: Registers the built-in benchmark, function, LLM-judge, ground-truth, SCM, RL and meta evaluators with lazily imported implementations.

nodes.name: get_evaluator_registry
nodes.summary: Returns the global EvaluatorRegistry singleton, creating it on first use.

nodes.name: reset_evaluator_registry
nodes.summary: Resets the global EvaluatorRegistry singleton so tests start from a clean registry.

nodes.name: EvaluatorRegistry

nodes.name: genomes.py

nodes.name: _register_builtin_genomes

nodes.summary: Resets the global OperatorRegistry singleton so tests start from a clean registry.

nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.name: scm_evaluator.py
nodes.summary: Multi-objective fitness evaluator for Structural Causal Model genomes: decodes SCMs, scores data fit, sparsity, simplicity, coverage and latent parsimony, and applies acyclicity, coverage and conflict penalties with several partial-evaluation strategies for cyclic graphs.
nodes.languageNotes: All evolve imports are deferred to TYPE_CHECKING or function scope to break circular imports between evaluation and representation.

nodes.name: result.py
nodes.summary: Frozen result container for meta-evolution runs holding the best configuration, fitness, solution and history, with Pareto-front extraction and JSON export of the best config.

nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.name: SymbiogeneticMerge
nodes.summary: Runtime-checkable protocol for operators that permanently absorb a symbiont genome into a host, producing one merged offspring and rejecting identical instances.

nodes.name: CrossoverOperator

nodes.name: UniformCrossover

nodes.name: SinglePointCrossover

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the Evolvable Reproduction Protocols (ERP) module, re-exporting protocol data types, matchability/intent/crossover evaluators, protocol mutation, recovery strategies and sandboxing helpers; ERPEngine is deliberately left out to avoid circular imports.

nodes.name: crossover_protocol.py
nodes.summary: Implements the crossover half of ERP: pluggable crossover executors (single-point, two-point, uniform, BLX-alpha blend, clone), a type-keyed registry, step-limited safe execution with clone fallback, 50/50 single-parent protocol inheritance, and offspring genome validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typing.Protocol (structural subtyping) for CrossoverExecutor; concrete executors never inherit it and are registered at import time into a class-level registry.

nodes.name: execute_crossover
nodes.summary: Runs a CrossoverProtocolSpec: clones parents when the spec is inactive, otherwise dispatches to the registered executor and raises on unknown types.

nodes.name: safe_execute_crossover
nodes.summary: Wraps execute_crossover with a fresh StepCounter and catches any failure, falling back to parent clones and returning a success flag.

nodes.name: inherit_protocol
nodes.summary: Chooses the offspring's reproduction protocol from exactly one parent with 50/50 probability, handling parents without protocols.

nodes.name: validate_offspring
nodes.summary: Checks an offspring genome's shape, dtype and finiteness (no NaN/Inf) against its parent before it may enter the population.

nodes.name: CrossoverExecutor
nodes.summary: Structural Protocol interface for crossover executors: produce two new offspring genomes from two parents, deterministically given the RNG, charging steps to a StepCounter.

nodes.name: SinglePointCrossoverExecutor
nodes.summary: Single-point crossover for array-like genomes, swapping tails after a random cut point.

nodes.name: TwoPointCrossoverExecutor
nodes.summary: Two-point crossover for array-like genomes, exchanging the segment between two random cut points.

nodes.name: UniformCrossoverExecutor
nodes.summary: Uniform crossover that swaps each gene independently with a configurable probability.

nodes.name: BlendCrossoverExecutor
nodes.summary: BLX-alpha blend crossover for real-valued genomes, sampling offspring genes from an interval expanded around the parents' values.

nodes.name: CloneCrossoverExecutor
nodes.summary: No-op crossover that returns copies of both parents; used for inactive specs and as the registry fallback.

nodes.name: CrossoverRegistry
nodes.summary: Class-level registry mapping CrossoverType values to executor instances, with lookup, clone-defaulting lookup and listing.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: Defines ERPConfig and ERPEngine, an EvolutionEngine subclass where each individual's encoded protocol governs mating: intent is checked before mutual matchability, offspring come from protocol-specified crossover, protocols are inherited and mutated, and recovery strategies prevent population collapse.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports core modules directly rather than via the package __init__ to break a circular import; ERPEngine overrides the base template-method hooks _step and _compute_metrics.

nodes.name: ERPConfig
nodes.summary: EvolutionConfig extension adding ERP parameters: per-evaluation step limit, recovery threshold, protocol mutation rate, and switches for intent and recovery.

nodes.name: ERPEngine
nodes.summary: Evolution engine where mating requires both parents to be willing (intent) and to accept each other (matchability); builds offspring via protocol crossover with validation, inherits and mutates protocols, records ReproductionEvents, applies recovery on low success rates, and reports ERP metrics.

nodes.name: intent.py
nodes.summary: Implements reproduction intent policies that decide whether an individual is willing to reproduce (always/never, fitness or rank threshold, offspring budget, age window, probabilistic), with a string-keyed registry and step-limited safe evaluation.

nodes.name: evaluate_intent
nodes.summary: Evaluates a ReproductionIntentPolicy: inactive policies are willing, active ones dispatch to the registered evaluator, unknown types raise ValueError.

nodes.name: safe_evaluate_intent
nodes.summary: Evaluates intent under a fresh StepCounter, returning (willing, success) and treating overruns or errors as unwilling.

nodes.name: IntentEvaluator
nodes.summary: Structural Protocol interface for intent evaluators, returning whether an individual is willing to reproduce given an IntentContext and params.

nodes.name: AlwaysWillingIntent
nodes.summary: Intent evaluator that is always willing to reproduce; the registry default.

nodes.name: NeverWillingIntent
nodes.summary: Intent evaluator that never reproduces; useful to switch reproduction off for an individual.

nodes.name: FitnessThresholdIntent
nodes.summary: Willing to reproduce only when the individual's fitness meets a threshold.

nodes.name: FitnessRankThresholdIntent
nodes.summary: Willing to reproduce only when the individual's fitness rank is high enough.

nodes.name: ResourceBudgetIntent
nodes.summary: Willing to reproduce until the individual's offspring budget is exhausted.

nodes.name: AgeDependentIntent
nodes.summary: Willing to reproduce only within a configured age range.

nodes.name: ProbabilisticIntent
nodes.summary: Willing to reproduce with a fixed probability drawn from the RNG.

nodes.name: IntentRegistry
nodes.summary: Class-level registry mapping intent type strings to evaluators, defaulting to AlwaysWillingIntent for unknown types.

nodes.name: matchability.py
nodes.summary: Implements matchability evaluators that decide whether an individual accepts a potential mate (accept/reject all, distance or similarity thresholds, fitness ratio, niche difference, probabilistic, crowding-distance diversity seeking), plus a registry and step-limited safe evaluation.

nodes.name: evaluate_matchability
nodes.summary: Evaluates a MatchabilityFunction: inactive functions reject, active ones dispatch to the registry, and probabilistic results are resolved to a boolean with the RNG.

nodes.name: safe_evaluate_matchability
nodes.summary: Evaluates matchability under a fresh StepCounter, returning (accepted, success) and rejecting on overruns or errors.

nodes.name: MatchabilityEvaluator
nodes.summary: Structural Protocol interface for matchability evaluators, deciding (or giving a probability) whether a partner described by a MateContext is acceptable.

nodes.name: AcceptAllMatchability
nodes.summary: Matchability evaluator that accepts every potential mate.

nodes.name: RejectAllMatchability
nodes.summary: Matchability evaluator that rejects every potential mate; the registry fallback for unknown types.

nodes.name: DistanceThresholdMatchability
nodes.summary: Accepts mates whose genetic distance is at or above a threshold (outbreeding preference).

nodes.name: SimilarityThresholdMatchability
nodes.summary: Accepts mates whose genetic distance is below a threshold (assortative, similar mates).

nodes.name: FitnessRatioMatchability
nodes.summary: Accepts mates whose fitness ratio falls within a configured range.

nodes.name: DifferentNicheMatchability
nodes.summary: Accepts mates only from a different niche or species.

nodes.name: ProbabilisticMatchability
nodes.summary: Returns a clamped acceptance probability that grows with genetic distance from a base probability.

nodes.name: DiversitySeekingMatchability
nodes.summary: Prefers partners with high crowding distance for multi-objective diversity, with a fallback when crowding is unavailable.

nodes.name: MatchabilityRegistry
nodes.summary: Class-level registry mapping matchability type strings to evaluators, defaulting to RejectAllMatchability for unknown types.

nodes.name: mutation.py
nodes.summary: Protocol mutation operators that evolve reproduction strategies: Gaussian parameter mutation, strategy-type switching, activation toggling, and junk-data neutral drift with promotion/demotion between junk and active parameters, orchestrated by ProtocolMutator.

nodes.name: mutate_params
nodes.summary: Applies Gaussian noise to parameter values at a given rate and strength, clamping probability-like parameters.

nodes.name: add_random_param
nodes.summary: Adds a randomly named, randomly valued parameter to a params dict.

nodes.name: mutate_junk_data
nodes.summary: Neutral-drift mutation of junk data: randomly adds, removes or perturbs entries, including nested dictionaries.

nodes.name: promote_junk_to_param
nodes.summary: Moves a numeric junk-data entry into the active parameters, activating dormant logic.

nodes.name: demote_param_to_junk
nodes.summary: Moves an active parameter into junk data, preserving its value as dormant material.

nodes.name: mutate_matchability
nodes.summary: Mutates a MatchabilityFunction by switching its type, toggling its active flag and perturbing parameters.

nodes.name: mutate_intent
nodes.summary: Mutates a ReproductionIntentPolicy by switching its type, toggling activation and perturbing parameters.

nodes.name: mutate_crossover
nodes.summary: Mutates a CrossoverProtocolSpec by switching the crossover type, toggling activation and perturbing parameters.

nodes.name: MutationConfig
nodes.summary: Rates controlling protocol mutation: parameter noise rate and strength, type switching, activation toggling, and junk-data add/remove/modify/activate.

nodes.name: ProtocolMutator
nodes.summary: Main mutation interface: builds a new ReproductionProtocol by mutating each component and junk data (with optional junk promotion), or mutates a single named component.

nodes.name: protocol.py
nodes.summary: Core immutable data model for ERP: the CrossoverType enum, MateContext and IntentContext evaluation contexts, the evolvable MatchabilityFunction / ReproductionIntentPolicy / CrossoverProtocolSpec components, the composite ReproductionProtocol genome, and the ReproductionEvent audit record, all with dict serialization.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses make protocols immutable; __post_init__ marks NumPy fitness arrays read-only so evaluators cannot mutate shared state.

nodes.name: CrossoverType
nodes.summary: Enum of supported crossover strategies: single-point, two-point, uniform, blend, module exchange and clone.

nodes.name: MateContext
nodes.summary: Frozen context passed to matchability evaluators: partner distance, fitness rank and ratio, niche, population diversity, crowding distance, and read-only fitness arrays.

nodes.name: IntentContext
nodes.summary: Frozen context passed to intent evaluators: fitness, fitness rank, age, offspring count, generation and population size.

nodes.name: MatchabilityFunction
nodes.summary: Immutable, serializable evolvable component naming a matchability type, its params and an active flag.

nodes.name: ReproductionIntentPolicy
nodes.summary: Immutable, serializable evolvable component naming an intent type, its params and an active flag.

nodes.name: CrossoverProtocolSpec
nodes.summary: Immutable, serializable evolvable component naming a CrossoverType, its params and an active flag.

nodes.name: ReproductionProtocol
nodes.summary: The Reproduction Protocol Genome attached to individuals, combining matchability, intent and crossover components plus junk data, with serialization and an accept-all default factory.

nodes.name: ReproductionEvent
nodes.summary: Audit record of one reproduction attempt: generation, parents, success, failure reason, offspring ids, and per-parent intent and matchability results.

nodes.name: recovery.py
nodes.summary: Recovery strategies that keep ERP populations alive when selective protocols collapse the mating success rate: immigrant injection, temporary mutation boosts, temporary relaxed matching, and a composite that applies the first triggered strategy.

nodes.name: RecoveryStrategy
nodes.summary: Structural Protocol interface for recovery strategies: should_trigger on low mating success, and recover by adjusting the survivor population.

nodes.name: ImmigrationRecovery
nodes.summary: Injects freshly generated immigrants (new genome and protocol) when success rate drops below a threshold, respecting minimum generations and a cooldown.

nodes.name: MutationBoostRecovery
nodes.summary: Temporarily multiplies mutation rates for a fixed number of generations when mating success collapses.

nodes.name: RelaxedMatchingRecovery
nodes.summary: Temporarily relaxes matchability constraints for a few generations when mating success collapses.

nodes.name: CompositeRecovery
nodes.summary: Combines several recovery strategies, triggering if any does and applying the first one that triggers.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the experiment subsystem that re-exports configuration, checkpointing, metric trackers, the experiment runner, and dry-run cost-estimation types through __all__.

nodes.name: checkpoint.py
nodes.summary: Defines the picklable Checkpoint snapshot of population, RNG state, and generation plus a CheckpointManager that saves at intervals, loads latest/specific generations, and prunes old checkpoints.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Declares ExperimentConfig, a JSON-serializable, hashable dataclass capturing every experiment parameter, along with validation helpers and ConfigValidationError.

nodes.name: dry_run.py
nodes.summary: Dry-run cost estimator that micro-benchmarks each atomic evolutionary operation (evaluation, selection, crossover, mutation, merge, ERP, ranking, decoding, tracking) and multiplies by config-derived structural constants to project total runtime, memory, and bottlenecks without running evolution.

nodes.name: runner.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates reproducible experiment execution by wiring an EvolutionEngine to checkpointing, metric tracking, and stopping criteria, and provides experiment comparison and hyperparameter sweep utilities.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic dataclass (Generic[G]) with TYPE_CHECKING-only imports of engine and population types to avoid circular imports.

nodes.name: Checkpoint

nodes.name: CheckpointManager

nodes.name: ExperimentConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding all experiment parameters with dict/JSON round-tripping, SHA-256 content hashing for deduplication, validation, and copy-with-overrides.

nodes.name: ConfigValidationError

nodes.name: validate_config
nodes.summary: Validates an ExperimentConfig and raises ConfigValidationError when any errors are reported.

nodes.name: PhaseEstimate
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass recording one benchmarked phase: per-call time, calls per generation, projected total, share of runtime, and bottleneck flag.

nodes.name: ComputeResources

nodes.name: MemoryEstimate
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass with projected genome, population, and total memory usage.

nodes.name: MetaEstimate
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass projecting meta-evolution cost: outer generations, trials, and total inner runs.

nodes.name: DryRunReport

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to see what Evolve Framework is: a research-grade toolkit for evolutionary algorithms covering single- and multi-objective optimization, NEAT-style neuroevolution, Evolvable Reproduction Protocols (ERP) and experiment tracking. Its quick start shows the three calls every experiment is built from: declare a UnifiedConfig, build an engine with create_engine(), and call engine.run() on a population from create_initial_population(). The rest of this tour follows that exact path through the code.

tour.title: Design Principles and Packaging
tour.description: Before reading code, learn the rules it obeys. The constitution lists eight principles (model-agnostic core, separation of concerns, declarative completeness, optional acceleration, determinism, extensibility, multi-domain support, observability), and evolve/agents.md turns them into concrete package rules: no ML-framework imports in core, NumPy-only numerics and immutable genomes. pyproject.toml enforces this at install time by keeping core dependencies to NumPy and NetworkX and moving PyTorch, JAX, MLflow, W&B, Ray and RL support into optional extras.
tour.languageLesson: pyproject.toml's [project.optional-dependencies] tables define installable extras, so `pip install evolve-framework[pytorch]` pulls in extra packages only for users who ask for them. This is how a Python library stays light by default while still offering heavy optional integrations.

tour.title: UnifiedConfig: One Declarative Spec
tour.description: UnifiedConfig is the single object that describes an entire experiment: population size, operators and their parameters, genome type, evaluator, decoder, and optional sub-configs for stopping, callbacks, ERP, multi-objective, meta-evolution and tracking. It is frozen, JSON-serializable and stably hashable, which is what makes the determinism principle from Step 2 practical, since a saved config reproduces a run. The package barrel re-exports every sub-config, and the schema module versions the config format so older saved files are rejected or migrated safely.
tour.languageLesson: `@dataclass(frozen=True)` makes instances immutable: fields cannot be reassigned after construction, and instances become safely hashable. Instead of mutating a config, the code builds modified copies (the with_* builders, typically via dataclasses.replace), a functional style that keeps a config's hash stable for its whole life.

tour.title: The Factory: Config to Engine
tour.description: create_engine() is the bridge between the declarative config from Step 3 and a runnable engine, and it sits at the root of the dependency graph (depth 0 of the traversal). It resolves the named evaluator, decoder, operators, callbacks and genome from the registries, checks that the chosen operators are compatible with the genome type, builds the stopping criteria, and then picks the right engine: a standard EvolutionEngine, an ERPEngine, or an NSGA-II multi-objective engine. create_initial_population() uses the same config to seed the first generation.

tour.title: Registries: Names to Implementations
tour.description: The strings in a UnifiedConfig, such as selection="tournament" or genome_type="vector", are turned into real objects by registries, which the factory from Step 4 queries. The OperatorRegistry stores selection, crossover, mutation and merge operators together with genome-compatibility metadata, while the GenomeRegistry and EvaluatorRegistry map names to factories with default parameters. Each registry registers its built-ins lazily behind a global singleton, and user code can register its own entries, which is how the framework meets its extensibility principle.
tour.languageLesson: The registry pattern uses a dictionary from a name to a factory callable, usually behind a module-level singleton accessor such as get_operator_registry(). Lazily registering built-ins on first access avoids import cycles and keeps optional dependencies from loading until someone actually asks for them.

tour.title: Core Types: Fitness, Individual, Population
tour.description: core/types.py has the highest fan-in in the codebase (85 files link to it), because every other part speaks its vocabulary: a vector-valued Fitness that supports constraints, Pareto dominance and Deb's feasibility-first comparison, plus the immutable, generic Individual that pairs a genome with its fitness and metadata. Population is an immutable container of individuals with cached statistics and feasibility-aware best-individual lookup. Learn these two files first, because the operators, engines and collectors in later steps all take and return these types.
tour.languageLesson: Python generics such as `Individual[G]` (built with TypeVar and Generic) let a single class carry any genome type while type checkers still track which one. Combined with frozen dataclasses, an Individual[VectorGenome] can be neither modified nor accidentally mixed with an Individual[GraphGenome].

tour.title: Genome Representations
tour.description: A genome is what evolution actually changes, and the framework ships several immutable representations for different problem domains. VectorGenome (a fixed-length, bounded real-valued array) is the default and third most depended-on file; SequenceGenome supports genetic programming; GraphGenome implements NEAT-style topology evolution with innovation numbers; EmbeddingGenome evolves LLM soft-prompt embeddings; and SCMGenome encodes causal graphs for causal discovery. The GenomeRegistry from Step 5 is what maps genome_type names to these classes.

tour.title: Variation Operators
tour.description: Selection, crossover and mutation are defined as protocols with concrete implementations: tournament, roulette and rank selection with feasibility-first ranking; uniform, point, BLX-alpha and SBX crossover for vectors plus innovation-aligned crossover for NEAT graphs; and Gaussian, polynomial and structural mutations. A symbiogenetic merge operator lets one graph genome absorb another's hidden topology. These operators consume the Population and Fitness types from Step 6 and act on the genomes from Step 7, which is why the OperatorRegistry records which genomes each operator supports.
tour.languageLesson: typing.Protocol defines structural interfaces: any class with the right method signatures satisfies the protocol, with no inheritance required. This lets users plug in their own selection or mutation operator without importing or subclassing any framework base class.

tour.title: Evaluation and Execution Backends
tour.description: Fitness evaluation is usually the most expensive part of a run, so the Evaluator protocol is designed as the framework's main acceleration boundary. FunctionEvaluator wraps a per-individual function, such as the pure-NumPy benchmarks (sphere, Rastrigin, ZDT) used in the README quick start, while BatchEvaluator scores whole populations at once. Execution backends then decide where the work runs: sequentially, across CPU cores with deterministic per-batch seeds, or on a GPU through the optional PyTorch backend, which is only imported when installed, in line with Step 2's principles.

tour.title: The Evolution Loop
tour.description: EvolutionEngine brings everything together: each generation it evaluates the population (Step 9), selects and varies with the operators (Step 8), replaces the old generation, and checks whether to stop, using an explicit RNG so runs are reproducible. Callbacks hook into loop events for printing, history, logging, checkpointing and hall-of-fame archives, and stopping criteria cover generation limits, fitness thresholds, stagnation and wall-clock time. This is the engine.run() call from the README, and the ERP and multi-objective variants in the next steps build on it.

tour.title: Multi-Objective Optimization
tour.description: When an experiment has several competing objectives, MultiObjectiveConfig declares them (with directions, weights and constraints) and the factory from Step 4 builds an NSGA-II engine. These files form a tightly coupled cluster: MultiObjectiveFitness holds raw objective vectors and constraint violations, dominance.py implements constrained Pareto dominance, and ranking.py performs NSGA-II's fast non-dominated sort into ranked fronts. Crowding distance from the niching module breaks ties within a front, so the engine keeps a spread of trade-off solutions instead of one winner.

tour.title: Evolvable Reproduction Protocols
tour.description: ERP is the framework's most distinctive feature: each individual carries its own reproduction protocol, so mating strategy evolves alongside the solution. protocol.py defines the immutable protocol genome and its three parts (intent policies decide whether an individual wants to reproduce, matchability functions decide whether it accepts a given mate, and crossover specs decide how offspring are made). ERPEngine subclasses the EvolutionEngine from Step 10 to apply these rules, and adding ERPSettings to a UnifiedConfig is what makes the factory choose it.

tour.title: Diversity, Meta-Evolution and RL
tour.description: Several subsystems extend the basic loop for harder research problems. The island model runs subpopulations in parallel and migrates individuals between them over a configurable topology, and speciation groups similar genomes (including by NEAT compatibility distance) to protect innovation. Meta-evolution treats a UnifiedConfig itself as a genome: the codec encodes hyperparameters as vectors and MetaEvaluator scores each candidate config by running seeded inner evolution trials. RLEvaluator decodes genomes into policies and scores them by episode rollouts, which enables neuroevolution for control tasks.

tour.title: Experiment Tracking and Metrics
tour.description: Observability comes from pairing a TrackingConfig (backend, URI, buffering, sampling, and minimal, standard or comprehensive presets) with a TrackingCallback that plugs into the engine's callback system from Step 10. The callback logs per-generation metrics, config parameters and the best solution to MLflow through a resilient tracker that buffers metrics while the server is unreachable. The metrics come from collectors that share one MetricCollector protocol and CollectionContext, one collector per subsystem (ERP, islands, NEAT, Pareto fronts and others); the reference guide documents every metric they emit.

tour.title: Tutorials, Tests and CI
tour.description: The seven tutorial notebooks make a guided path through everything covered here, starting with 01_unified_config, which mirrors this tour's config-factory-engine flow. The tests/ tree mirrors the evolve/ layout, and conftest.py supplies the seeded RNG fixtures that keep tests deterministic. The CI workflow runs the core test matrix across Ubuntu and macOS with Python 3.10 to 3.12, separate PyTorch, JAX, RL and notebook jobs, ruff and mypy, and a guard that core modules never import ML frameworks, which enforces Step 2's constitution automatically.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows fire on `on:` triggers (here push and pull request), run `jobs` in parallel, and use a `strategy.matrix` to fan one job out across operating systems and Python versions. Keeping optional-backend tests in their own jobs lets the core suite pass without PyTorch or JAX installed.
